extracted.intended_audience: researchers, patent applicants and patent agents seeking to deposit biological material (microorganisms, plasmids, phages, cell lines, seeds) under the Budapest Treaty; collections' depositors
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical standards used by multiple culture collections for accepting, preserving, testing viability of, and furnishing biological deposits made for patent purposes under the Budapest Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted acceptance of certain pathogenic PG I bacteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The following bacteria of pathogenic group I (PG I: World Health Organization (WHO)) are accepted only when they can be maintained by the Rijks Instituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieuhygiene (RIVM), Centraal Diergeneeskundig Instituut (CDI) or the Royal Institute for Tropical Research: Bordetella (all species), Brucella (all species), Erysipelothrix (all species), Leptospira (all species), Listeria (all species), Mycobacterium paratuberculosis, Pasteurella (all species), Treponema (all species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance conditional on ability of specified national institutes (RIVM, CDI, Royal Institute) to maintain the organisms; depositors must consult/arrange accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted acceptance of certain PG II bacteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The following bacteria of pathogenic group II (PG II (WHO)) are accepted only when they can be maintained by RIVM or CDI: Bartonella (all species), Francisella (all species), Mycobacterium bovis, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Pseudomonas mallei, Pseudomonas pseudomallei.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance only if those national institutes can maintain them; contact those institutes in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain highly dangerous bacteria not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: The following bacteria are not accepted: Bacillus anthracis and Yersinia pestis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such organisms are excluded from deposit at this collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred form of deposit (lyophilized preferred; alternatives accepted)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBS (and other collections) prefers to receive microorganisms submitted for deposit as lyophilized preparations. Where it is undesirable or impossible to supply lyophilized preparations, active cultures growing in or on a suitable nutrient medium are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lyophilization cannot be supplied, collections may accept active cultures; depositor should note collection preferences and contact for special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and minimum quantity/replicates per deposit type (CBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum number of replicates required by CBS when making a deposit: Fungi: 12 lyophilized cultures or 2 agar cultures; Yeasts: 12 lyophilized plus 1 agar culture or 2 agar cultures; Bacteria: 12 lyophilized plus 1 agar culture or 3 agar cultures; Plasmids (in hosts): 12 lyophilized plus 1 agar culture or 3 agar cultures; Plasmids (purified DNA): minimum quantity of 50 µg; Phages: 10 ml with a titre of at least 10^9 pfu/ml.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must supply specified minimum replicates in the specified forms; where depositor unable to supply lyophilized material CBS can prepare it (fees apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection-prepared preservation services and fees (CBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: If depositor is unable to supply lyophilized preparations, the CBS prepares lyophilized cultures at the time of deposit from material supplied by the depositor at a fee of Euro 125 for a batch of 10 ampoules; when material cannot be freeze-dried, CBS prepares a batch of 10 frozen straws at a fee of Euro 175. Preparation of a phage lysate with a sufficiently high titre can be done at a fee of Euro 500. Plasmid stocks are not prepared by the CBS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must check authenticity of the prepared batch; CBS charges set fees for preparation services; plasmid stocks must be supplied by depositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor must check authenticity of batches prepared by collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositor is required to check the authenticity of a sample of the batch prepared by the CBS (and similarly by other collections) and to inform the collection of the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections routinely ask depositors to check authenticity after transfers/subculturing; new batches are prepared when stocks diminish; a portion of the original material is always kept by the collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time required for viability testing (CBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average length of time required for testing viability given by type: Fungi, bacteria, plasmids in hosts or purified DNA, phages: 2 weeks; Yeasts: 1 week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasionally testing may take longer, especially if unusual antibiotics or additives are necessary. For plasmids, the 'viability test' consists of transforming a suitable host; if the host is transformed, the viability test is regarded as positive.

rubrics_metrics.name: General language policy for deposit communications (CBS/IAFB/PCM/KACC/KCLRF)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS official language is English; communications also accepted in Dutch, German and French (preferred English). IAFB official language Polish, communications in English or Russian accepted. PCM official language Polish, communications in English accepted. KACC official languages Korean and English. KCLRF official language Korean, correspondence may be in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should use the collection's accepted languages and prefer the stated preferred language for correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor contract/withdrawal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections do not enter into a written contract defining liabilities; by signing the collection deposit forms the depositor surrenders any right to withdraw his deposit during the required storage period and accepts that the microorganism will be distributed according to the relevant patent requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor should understand that signing accession forms removes right to withdraw and accepts distribution obligations under patent law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and quarantine regulations requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain microorganisms are subject to import and/or quarantine regulations. The collection will advise depositors about these and will make arrangements for transportation and, if necessary, licenses (fees on request). Contact the collection in advance for precise instructions; for plant pathogens further information may be obtained from specific national plant pathology authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must contact collection in advance for organisms that may be subject to regulatory controls, especially for international shipments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific plant pathogenic bacteria requiring advance contact (CBS list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBS should be contacted in advance if deposit of any of the following plant pathogenic bacteria is intended: Agrobacterium rhizogenes, Corynebacterium flaccumfaciens, C. insidiosum, C. michiganense, C. sepedonicum, Erwinia amylovora, E. stewartii, E. tracheiphila, Pseudomonas caryophylli, P. solanacearum, P. syringae (various pathovars), P. woodsii, Xanthomonas ampelina, X. campestris (various pathovars), X. fragariae, X. populi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must contact CBS for instructions and possible quarantine/import arrangements before deposit of listed plant pathogens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required accession and amendment forms (BP/1, BP/7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositor is required to complete the CBS accession form for patent deposits and model form BP/1. In the event of a later indication or amendment of the scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation, the depositor must complete model form BP/7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mandatory model forms (BP series) as specified by the collection for original deposits and later amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notification forms for receipt and viability (BP/4, BP/9, BP/8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receipt and viability statement are issued on mandatory 'international forms' BP/4 and BP/9, respectively. Attestation of receipt of a later indication or amendment is issued on form BP/8. Standard forms are not used for other official notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections will issue these standard international forms for official records; depositors can request unofficial early communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial notifications (provisional communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, collections will telephone or telex/e-mail the date of deposit and accession number after receipt and the result of the viability test before the official statements are issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional information can be provided on request but is subject to official verification and final statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of information to a patent agent (collection policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections vary: CBS does not ask for the name/address of the patent agent and will supply copies of the receipt and viability statement either to the depositor or to his patent agent, but not to both. IAFB may send copies to both if requested. PCM will send to patent agent if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor should indicate preferences for who receives official documents; collections have differing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of previous non-Budapest deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits made outside the provisions of the Budapest Treaty may be converted by the original depositor to Budapest Treaty deposits; administrative requirements for conversion are the same as those for an original deposit (with some exceptions for import/quarantine or previous EPC deposits). Converted deposits are subject to storage fees normally levied for Budapest Treaty deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion possible but may require additional documentation and fees; check collection-specific conditions (e.g., KACC requires original receipt copy for conversion if originally made for patent purposes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for making a new deposit (BP/2 and Rule 6.2 documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a new deposit, the depositor is required to complete model form BP/2 and to send copies of the relevant documents (Rule 6.2); otherwise procedure similar to original deposit. Receipt and viability statements for a new deposit may be issued on BP/5 and BP/9 respectively (collection-specific).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow BP/2 and provide required supporting documents to effect a new deposit; collections will issue appropriate BP forms for new deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice and provision of request forms to third parties (BP/12 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections advise third parties of the correct procedures to make a valid request. For requests requiring proof of entitlement, the collection will provide copies of model request form BP/12 and/or request forms used by individual industrial property offices (where provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties requesting samples should follow the model request forms; collections assist in ensuring requests are valid for patent-scope access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence verification before release of hazardous samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding entitlement under patent regulations, in the case of potentially hazardous microorganisms the collection will first confirm that the requesting party is competent to handle them. Samples are not released to private persons not engaged in a relevant profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections will withhold potentially dangerous organisms until competence and appropriate credentials are verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption about import requirements for overseas requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding to requests from overseas, the collection assumes that the requesting party has met the import requirements of his own country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility for complying with destination-country import/quarantine rules lies with the requester; collection may not verify foreign compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of samples furnished (collection-prepared vs depositor-supplied)
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples of yeasts and bacteria furnished by the CBS are usually from batches of its own preparations, but samples of other microorganisms are usually from preparations supplied by the depositor. KACC furnishes samples from batches of its own preparations in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections differ in whether samples originate from their own preserved batches or from depositor-supplied material; requesters/depositors should note the collection's practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of depositor when samples furnished; option to waive
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless he has waived his right to be so notified, the collection notifies the depositor by letter when samples of his microorganisms have been furnished to third parties. The collection offers a reduced fee for storage to depositors who waive their right to be notified of the release of samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors may waive notification in exchange for reduced storage fees; otherwise they will be informed on release of samples (usually BP/14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing of Budapest Treaty deposits (not listed publicly)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBS/IAFB/PCM/KACC do not list Budapest Treaty deposits in their published catalogue or list of cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budapest Treaty deposits are normally excluded from public catalogues; depositors should not expect public listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees (CBS example: storage, preparation, viability statements, furnishing samples)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS fee schedule examples: Storage (30 years) EUR 650; Conversion EUR 650; Preservation of stock material (set of 10 ampoules freeze-dried) EUR 125; set of 10 frozen straws EUR 175; Issuance of a viability statement EUR 80 (if viability test carried out) or EUR 25 (based on last viability test); Communication of information EUR 100; Attestation EUR 40; Furnishing of a sample (agar slant EUR 15; freeze-dried ampoule EUR 10); Surcharge to cover bank and administrative costs EUR 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections publish fee schedules; fees may vary by collection, service type, and do not include transport or bank fees. Depositors should consult the specific collection's fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance availability for depositors
rubrics_metrics.description: Some collections (e.g., CBS) do not produce a standard letter or guidance notes but provide guidance in newsletters or on request. Others (PCM, IAFB, KACC, KCLRF) offer advice by telephone, fax or e-mail and may not have standard written guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective depositors should contact collections for specific advice; written guidance may be limited or intermittent.

rubrics_metrics.name: IAFB acceptance criteria (kinds of microorganisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: IAFB accepts bacteria, yeasts and filamentous fungi which are capable of long-term preservation without any substantial change in their initial properties. Note: dangerous pathogens and species hazardous to man and animals will not be accepted; microorganisms with special cultivation requirements the collection cannot carry out will not be accepted; mixtures and cultures without scientific description or that cannot be identified will not be accepted; strains containing plasmids accepted only if plasmid and host are group P1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IAFB imposes safety, technical capability, and identification requirements; plasmids accepted only for group P1 hosts/ plasmids.

rubrics_metrics.name: IAFB form and minimum quantity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: IAFB prefers lyophilized preparations. Minimum number of replicates: 20 for lyophilized preparations or three active cultures (agar slants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lyophilized not possible, active cultures acceptable; depositors must meet minimum replicate counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: IAFB viability testing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Average length of time for testing viability at IAFB is 7 to 14 days, though may take longer for unusual media or additives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should expect variability in testing time depending on organism and media requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCM acceptance criteria (kinds of microorganisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCM accepts bacteria (including actinomycetes) and bacteriophages capable of long-term preservation without substantial change. Note: dangerous pathogens and hazardous species will be conditionally accepted; special cultivation requirements not supported will not be accepted; mixtures, unidentified cultures not accepted; plasmids accepted only if plasmid and host group P1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCM applies safety and technical capability screening; depositors with plasmids must provide plasmid/host classification information.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCM form and minimum quantity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacteria (including those containing plasmids) must be submitted as lyophilized preparations or on culture transport media (not agar plates); minimum replicates: 10 lyophilized or on media or frozen (0.5 ml each). Bacteriophages: sufficient quantity and titre for preservation (at least 10^8 pfu/ml, 10 x 10 ml or 2 x 5 ml cell-free lysate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replicates should be from same batch and material must be free of contamination; depositor required to check authenticity of sample batch prepared by PCM.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCM viability testing times
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time required: Bacteria 3 days (or up to 14 days); Actinomycetes and other slow-growing organisms 5 days (or up to 20 days); Bacteriophages 7 days (or up to 14 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Times are average; slow-growers and special cases may take longer as indicated in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: KACC acceptance risk group restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: KACC accepts only organisms belonging to risk groups 1 or 2, in accordance with Directive 2000/54/EC. KACC reserves the right to refuse deposit of any material which in its view represents an unacceptable hazard or which it cannot process. KACC must be consulted in advance about conditions for acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must confirm organism risk group and consult KACC in advance for borderline or hazardous materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: KACC form and minimum quantity requirements (including seeds and viruses)
rubrics_metrics.description: KACC accepts lyophilized or frozen submissions. Minimum replicates: Bacteria, fungi, yeasts, mushroom, bacteria containing plasmid: 10; Bacteriophages: 10 ml (at least 10^9 pfu/ml); Plant viruses: 10 g lyophilized/dried material with host; Plant seeds: 1000 seeds (fresh, healthy, undamaged, <5% empty seeds; normally germination rate at least 85%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed deposits have additional quality/germination expectations; exceptions may be accepted where regeneration rate impossible; contact KACC for specific conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: KACC viability testing times
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time for viability testing: Bacteria, fungi, yeasts, mushroom, bacteria containing plasmid, plant viruses, bacteriophages: 14 days (or up to 30 days). Plant seeds: depends entirely on kind of seed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viability testing for seeds varies by species and may be substantially longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: KACC preparation of batches and depositor responsibility for some materials
rubrics_metrics.description: KACC prepares its own batches in lyophilized or frozen form at time of deposit by subculturing depositor material and generally does not prepare its own batches of viruses, bacteriophages and seeds—depositor is responsible for replenishing stock to ensure availability for required period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For items KACC does not reprepare, depositor must ensure sufficient stock remains available for distribution requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: KACC fees and service charges (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example KACC fees: Deposit (including initial viability check, preservation and storage for 30 years) original deposit KRW 800,000; new deposit KRW 70,000; Furnishing of a sample KRW 100,000; Issuance of a viability statement KRW 70,000 (if test requested) or KRW 10,000 (on basis of most recent test); Issuance of an attestation KRW 10,000; Communication of information KRW 10,000. Fees do not include transport costs or bank fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees vary by collection and service; check current fee schedules and note exclusions such as transport/bank fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: KCLRF acceptance criteria for cell lines and nucleic acids
rubrics_metrics.description: KCLRF accepts cell lines (human, animal, plant and hybridomas), eukaryotic DNA, plasmids (in hosts or not in hosts), EXCEPT: cell lines having properties which are or may be hazardous to human health and/or the environment; cell lines which have special requirements for experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KCLRF will not accept hazardous cell lines or those requiring unsupported special experimental conditions; contact in advance if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: KCLRF form and minimum replicates for cell lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, cell lines submitted to KCLRF for deposit should be in the form of frozen and viable culture. All cell lines should be free of contaminants. Minimum number of replicates required by the depositor: Cell lines in frozen form: 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must supply contaminant-free frozen viable cultures and provide at least the minimum number of replicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: KCLRF viability testing time and depositor checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time required for testing viability of cell lines: 14 days (or up to 28 days). KCLRF prepares its own batches in frozen form at time of deposit by subculturing the microorganism supplied by the depositor. New batches are prepared as necessary thereafter. Depositor required to check authenticity of samples of all batches prepared by KCLRF. KCLRF stores a portion of the original material supplied by the depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor involvement in authenticity checking is required; testing times may extend for specific cases.
